Our Light Up a Life tree is in the window again this year.

Some of you asked in the autumn whether we were doing it again, so I will say it plainly: yes, we are.

Seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it, my hand would not keep steady. Now I write it at the counter in the shop, with the same pen I have always used. The tree is for anyone who is grieving — it is not only for hospice families. If you have lost somebody and you would like to write their name on a tag and hang it in our window, then that is what the tree is for, and there is nothing else to qualify.

The details, if you would like them:

Memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November. The suggested donation is £3, and there are envelopes on the counter if you would rather write at home. Every penny goes to hospice care.

The tree goes up on Saturday 28 November, and we switch the lights on at 4pm. Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols for us, and Doreen is doing the mince pies again. (They did not last past the first carol last year.)

Every name on every tag will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You do not have to come to the service for your name to be read. Some people would rather not come, and that is entirely all right.

The tree stays lit until Twelfth Night.

Please do come and stand by the tree. You do not have to buy anything to do that. Come in, stand a while, and nobody will ask you a single question about it.

Last year the tree carried 412 tags. 412 names, every one of them somebody's person. Thank you to everyone who remembered with us, and to everyone who has sat with us through the year. I am not going to put a figure on what that meant. I will just say it was the best of our winter.

We keep every tag, bundled up with string, and they go back to the hospice to be kept safe.

Jean

Hello Hilary — yes, we are doing the tree again, and your mother's name would be very welcome on it for a second year. Tags will be on the counter in the shop from Monday 16 November (£3 suggested, and there are envelopes if you would rather write at home), and we switch the lights on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only hospice families, so you and your sister are very welcome to come and stand by it — you do not need to buy anything to do that. And every name gets read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, though she does not have to be there for her name to be read.

To: dm:moira.blyth
Replying to: [s01]
Cc: none
Subject: Light Up a Life — draft post for you to look over

Moira, the Light Up a Life post is drafted and sitting as a draft on the page, so nothing goes up until you have read it. Dates, tags, envelopes, the choir, Doreen's mince pies and the service are all exactly as you sent them.

Two things I did my own way, so do say if you would rather not. I have thanked everyone for last year without a word about money — the 412 names does that job for me — and I have put a few lines in about Ray, because it is seven years this month and people coming into the shop might like to know why the tree matters to us. Say the word and I will take it out.

I have also replied to Hilary on the page, just to say yes, we are doing it and the tags start on the 16th, so she knows to come with her sister. I have not used her name in the post itself.

Have a look whenever you have a minute.
